newsitem.title: USA: Hills Stores sees lower Q4 gross margin rate.
newsitem.headline: Hills Stores sees lower Q4 gross margin rate.

text.p: Hills Stores Co said Friday it expects its gross margin rate in the fourth quarter to be down about 100 basis points from a year earlier.
The exact rate will depend on the seasonal clearance markdown results, January sales, and the results of the year-end physical inventories, the company said.
Hills said it will feel the effect of clearance markdowns in the fourth quarter that are higher than originally planned because of a sales shortfall and higher-than-planned inventories.

Gregory Raven, president and chief executive of Hills, said sales results for the Christmas period were "disappointing," largely because of the five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year.

"The higher level of inventories means that our excess cash at year-end will be somewhat lower than we had earlier targeted. However, we still expect to be in a better excess cash position than at last year-end, with our overall liquidity during 1997 remaining much better than 1996," Raven said in a statement.

The discount retailer said it expects the fourth-quarter drop in margin rates on a year-to-year basis to be less significant than during the third quarter, when the deterioration was about 160 basis points.
